      TOOLS-GITHUB-ACTIONS-MONITOR 1.8.1

      Watches the workflows of every repository you own and shows what is red, stuck or waiting on one local page, in eight languages, with metrics for Grafana. A workflow is red when the last completed run of its file on the default branch failed; this dashboard uses the same rule (see the Sentinel tab).

      Two editions

      Complete: the monitor and the sentinel with its thirteen checks A1 to A13 (builds, red CI, security alerts, Dependabot pull requests, releases, hygiene, usage, rounds, roadmaps, the surface of Actions, readiness, analytics and the workflow linter).

      Lite: the monitor alone, with no sentinel; the connection with an AI tool is the same in both editions.

      Connect an AI tool

      Five channels, the same in both editions: a brief of what to do now, a feed of alerts, the state as data, a stream of events and MCP tools, plus a gate script that adds the brief to the session of the AI. Everything is read only unless you allow an action.

      Guide: connect an AI tool

      Quota and refresh

      The monitor spends little: conditional reads (an unchanged answer, a 304, costs nothing), batched GraphQL queries and saved reads. The central panel of this page is refreshed at least every half hour, and the Sentinel tab warns when it is more than two hours behind.

      Guide: more quota, less spending

      In the next version

      Not published yet: the panels A1 to A13 as data with one inventory of signals (act, watch, info), a Low mode that saves the allowance, the central panel of this page as a base line that spends no allowance, an optional read-only GitHub App with an allowance of its own, and a used-up allowance reported as one notice instead of one error per repository.

      Real action-token encoding/decoding (OpenVLA/RT-2-style 256-bin discretization per action dimension) and trajectory generation (delta-pose integration, absolute gripper state) - the 'Action Tokens' and 'Trajectory Generator' steps of the VLA flow, exposed via 'tokens encode'/'tokens decode'/'trajectory integrate'. A real, versioned model manifest contract (model_manifest.py) plus shape/confidence validation for a future model's inference output, and an honest 'status' subcommand reporting real accelerator/model-weight availability (never a fake ready state). Real VLA model inference still needs a real .hef model and a physical Hailo-10 module, both future work. Evidence is host-test: the automated test suite runs in CI on the host; nothing here has run against a simulator bench or real hardware.

      HYDRA-UMC-WATCH
      Actions Issues
      		UI Functional android Wearable 0.3.3 OK
      Version successfully resolved
      		Show the phase and the percent of a flash cycle on the screen (#16)
      Notes
      Functional v0: differentiated haptic vibration patterns wired to Wear OS Vibrator, explicit microphone/system-STT capture and local TTS confirmation, plus typed voice_turn/assistant_reply/system_status messages. A paired Android Data Layer relay is implemented; it keeps the Server JWT on the phone and Voice UI token on CM5. Physical radio, wireless E-STOP and live CM5 telemetry remain hardware integration gates. Voice never directly actuates a robot. The relay now has a real, testable reconnection policy (RelayRetryPolicy) and a last-known-state cache with staleness tracking (LastKnownStateCache) so a stale relayed status/alert is never shown as current. The relay now only ever sends to a real CapabilityClient-verified companion node (hydra_umc_phone_companion, not any connectedNodes.firstOrNull()), preferring a nearby node over a cloud-relayed one, and cancels a pending retry outright once the screen closes instead of only bounding it by attempt count. Evidence is simulator: the Wear OS workflows install the debug APK on an emulator and run the instrumented tests there (started by hand); no run on a real watch is recorded.

      HYDRA-UMC-SERVER
      Actions Issues
      		API Functional node CM5 0.8.3.0 OK
      Version successfully resolved
      		Run the container bench on the pull requests that touch what it covers (#28)
      Notes
      The real headless backend every control client (STUDIO, SUITE, DSI, the mobile apps) actually talks to.       Actions Issues
      		Service Functional python Dev Server 0.2.6 OK

      		Check the server bench out into its own folder so that another repository can call it (#14)
      Notes
      Functional - DS01-DS10 of the 10-delivery plan, now complete (contracts, limits and a verifiable skeleton). DS01-DS03 only read and describe. DS01: state-ownership table + 17-relationship grouping + a real, tested configuration schema (config.py) whose default policy grants NO task deployment permission. DS02: validated remote-station profile + read-only host preflight + dry-run provisioning plan, never executed. DS03: conservative migration (migration.py) - hashes/classifies every file in a source checkout, records unpushed commits, plans each class into one of four provably-separate destinations, refuses a private file to a shareable root; the source is never touched. DS04: the first thing that executes - workspace.py refuses a path that escapes a per-task workspace (.., absolute, symlink-out) and refuses two tasks sharing one; recipe.py pins a revision and refuses any command not in the policy's own allowed_commands; runner.py runs that one allow-listed command in the isolated workspace with a SCRUBBED environment (no inherited *_TOKEN/*_KEY/*_SECRET/ANTHROPIC_*/GITHUB_*/SSH_*), under a bounded timeout, killing the whole process group on timeout or cancel - proven by a real test that spawns a child-of-a-child and confirms both die. It still deploys nothing. Injectable WorkspaceFs/ProcessLauncher seams keep the control tests off a real host. DS05: a durable SQLite queue (durable_queue.py) with leases and an append-only execution journal that survive a restart - a duplicate enqueue never becomes a second job, a crashed worker's lease expires and reconcile() returns the task to queued, a result from a worker that no longer holds the lease is rejected (never a false success), a base that moved since enqueue blocks promotion even on exit 0, and the journal keeps only bounded tails. DS06: an interchangeable AI provider behind a safety contract (ai_provider.py) - only the DETERMINISTIC FAKE ships (kind must be "fake"; a real provider and its authorization are a user decision). run_provider_step() turns a provider timeout / quota exhaustion / malformed output into a bounded named outcome (never an escalating exception), stops before a configured calls/tokens/cost budget would be exceeded, and treats the provider's answer as DATA never instructions - an "ignore previous instructions / deploy now / grant me root" suggestion is copied verbatim, flagged, and still grants_no_permissions / triggers_no_deploy for every outcome; the result is inert (wired to nothing). DS07: an authenticated incident transport (incident_transport.py) for the round trip with HYDRA-UMC-OPS-AGENT - every message is HMAC-signed by a registered node with a nonce, timestamp and contract version; verify_message() rejects an unregistered identity, a bad signature, a node impersonating another, a replayed nonce, a stale timestamp, an overloaded sender and an incompatible version, each with a named code. IncidentSession runs the full submit -> diagnosis -> post-deploy-verification round trip (not just the submit); a dropped connection leaves it pending-ack and reconcile() re-sends the same incident with a fresh nonce, the peer de-duping on the stable incident_id so nothing is lost or double-counted. It is a real protocol object, never a manual file drop. DS08: one fully controlled repair cycle (repair_cycle.py) chaining repro-confirmed -> incident-raised -> candidate-received -> regression-passed -> build-test-passed -> approved -> installed -> verified (or -> recovered / -> blocked). Every step is gated: an unreproduced failure never opens the cycle; a candidate whose HMAC signature does not verify, or that is pinned to a different incident / base fingerprint / target, is blocked; regression and build-test must be genuinely green; an approval must be signed by a registered approver AND issued for this exact base and target; install goes through an injectable isolated-installer seam (never the real target); a failed post-install verification rolls back and ends the cycle recovered, and the I60/T07 apparent-success control voids the result (with rollback) if the base moved mid-cycle or the evidence is for a different repro case. DS09: stable operation + verified restore (operations.py) - create_backup() records a sha256 per file with a backup_id, instance_id and schema_version; verify_backup() re-hashes and flags drift; restore_backup() refuses a backup for a different instance id or schema version, or one whose files no longer match, otherwise restores the exact bytes. check_operational_health() reports a named finding for orphaned (expired-but-leased) entries, a journal over its row cap, and free disk under the floor. All filesystem contact is behind the injectable BackupFs seam. DS10: the delivery package + an HONEST maturity evaluation (delivery.py). build_delivery_manifest() enumerates what the repo actually ships (every module/doc/config plus pyproject/manifest/CHANGELOG/README) with a sha256 per file, and reads back the real CLI surface, version and test count. evaluate_maturity() reports each of the ten deliveries as shipped/partial/not-started against real evidence (DS06 is partial on purpose - only the deterministic fake ships), lists seven known limitations in plain words, and hard-codes overall_maturity to "functional" - the code has no branch that returns anything higher, so the evaluation cannot over-claim. CLI: config / inventory / station / migrate / task / queue / provider / incident / repair / ops / deliver subcommands. The ten-delivery plan is complete; the maturity is "functional" (built and covered by tests, not verified on real hardware or services) - nothing here provisions a host, runs a deploy, or has touched target hardware, and `deliver evaluate` says exactly that. Evidence is simulator: the bench workflows start the swarm cell as real containers, run the bridges in front of an emulator and a Moonraker stand-in, and drive a simulated tool head on a virtual CAN bus, each with named scenarios that include refused and malformed input; no run on real hardware is recorded.

      Python 3.11+JSON Schemasystemd (host role, Linux only)SQLite (durable task/state journal, from DS05 onward)

      Two roles in one package: the edge role (deployed on a CM5) collects a real, sanitized inventory (installed project versions, service health checks, redacted logs) and derives read-only observations; the control-plane role (deployed on a development host, e.g. a Raspberry Pi 5) renders a saved snapshot, asks a provider-agnostic AI provider (Anthropic and/or OpenAI, optional `[ai-anthropic]`/`[ai-openai]` extras) to propose a root-cause explanation, manages a human-approved change proposal, applies a change approved with an Ed25519 signature to a staged clone and promotes it only if that project's own real build-test passes (optionally stopping and health-checking a service around the swap, with automatic rollback), records everything in a hash-chained audit journal, and re-verifies the original check. Optional, off by default and configured in one file: an authenticated edge-to-control channel, incidents from the node watchdog, notifications to the MQTT broker, a canary across several nodes, a proposal drafted by a local model (always pending) and Prometheus metrics. Real build: python -m build (see pyproject.toml).

A real, genuinely uncommitted edit to an already-TRACKED file is a separate case - checked explicitly upfront and refused outright, never silently discarded via the same staging-clone path. Evidence is host-test: the automated test suite runs in CI on the host; nothing here has run against a simulator bench or real hardware.

      Its own real test suite (`pytest tests`) passes in full (the tests that need the optional `[sdk]` extra or real hardware and are not silently counted as passing). v0.0.4 - a second independent review pass found and fixed 4 more real issues: the capability gate now enforces a write/abort capability's own declared requiredPermission/requiredCellState/requiresHumanConfirmation and the manifest's own requiredSafetyGates (previously ignored - a call was gate-allowed on the generic SDK motion check alone, zero policy enforced); adapterId is now restricted to a safe charset and save_certification_record() independently verifies its resolved path stays inside the target directory (previously a path-traversal adapterId could write outside it); the certification store now creates records with real atomic O_CREAT|O_EXCL semantics, refusing to silently overwrite a different record under the same id (previously not actually append-only despite documenting it as such); the JSON-Schema-subset validator no longer accepts a bool as a number or raises on an invalid regex pattern/non-string required entry (previously it could crash or silently accept wrong-typed evidence). Deliveries 1-4 of the 4-delivery plan ("Esquema JSON, CLI validate y diez fixtures" / "Registro ... y endpoint read-only de catalogo" / "Integracion con SDK: validacion de capability + safety gate + evidencia" [P0] / "Certificar adaptadores uno a uno sobre sus maquinas" [P1][HARDWARE]). Complementary to HYDRA-UMC-OPS-AGENT (maintenance-incident lifecycle for the ecosystem's OWN components) - this one is about discovering, validating and safely invoking what an EXTERNAL machine/adapter can do, never about CAN/SPI/UART access or motor control directly (those stay owned by HYDRA-UMC-SERVER/SDK/MCU). Explicitly does not replace HYDRA-UMC-GATEWAY-INDUSTRIAL, HYDRA-UMC-OPCUA-SERVER, HYDRA-UMC-MQTT-BROKER or HYDRA-UMC-MTCONNECT-ADAPTER - it is a declarative registry/validator/gate ABOVE them, not a second protocol implementation. The ten fixtures reference those real projects (and the real bridge repos) as their own ownerProject, never an invented one. A capability whose mode is write/abort is rejected by the validator unless it also declares risk, requiredPermission, requiredCellState and timeoutMs - an explicit rule ("las acciones write nunca son seleccionables si falta una de esas condiciones"), enforced as a real, tested check. Delivery 3's own gate never reimplements HYDRA-UMC-SDK's safety logic - it calls the SDK's real `evaluate_job()` directly (a `read` capability skips the SDK entirely; `write`/`abort` map onto a documented, honestly-simplified single JobPhase - see sdk_gate.py's own module docstring for exactly why). Delivery 4's own certification log is real, append-only record-keeping of a human-attested evidence payload checked against the adapter's own evidenceSchema - it explicitly does NOT and cannot independently verify that evidence came from real hardware without the real hardware itself, which this development machine does not have; that gap is documented, not hidden.

      A gateway in front of the URTC CAN bus, for an installation that cannot keep the bus closed: only the identifiers a host may send (made from the protocol specification) cross towards the bus, dangerous ones (bootloader, persistent settings) are refused unless unlocked, the payload must be one the specification allows, the rate is limited, and a peer must prove it holds a session key (HMAC with a nonce and a counter, so nothing recorded can be replayed). Every protection can be switched off from the file or the command line and the program says so. It is tested on a PC, including end to end through an SLCAN bus against a virtual board. It has never been run with a real bus, adapter or board.

      EH3D-PHOENIX-LASER is the laser engraving program of the PHOENIX family (bright red phoenix), formerly EH3D-LASER-CAM. Scaffolding v0.0.3: a library and a command line that read a PNG or PGM image, turn it into dots (threshold, Floyd-Steinberg or Atkinson dithering) and write the G-code of a laser that burns line by line with M4 dynamic power, S0 while it travels, an overscan worked out from the acceleration and alternating directions, plus a power-against-feed calibration grid. It also reads SVG and DXF drawings and writes the G-code that cuts their contours (inside ones first, the width of the beam taken into account, tabs, several passes) and engraves their shapes with lines, with the settings of each layer in a file and the program checked line by line before it is given. A window (egui, built with the gui feature: open a picture or a drawing, see the passes of the laser, edit the table of layers, export) is written and its logic is tested, but it has not been looked at on a screen; nothing has been tried on a laser.

                                                                                    Roadmap

                                                                                    Not a feature timeline with dates - the real path every project in this ecosystem follows, and exactly where each one sits on it right now (see the Maturity section above for the live counts).

                                                                                    1. Scaffolding 23

                                                                                      Real, tested code exists, but a large part of the project is still a skeleton or an open plan, and nothing has been tried in its real context. A project can finish its own plan and stay here until it is proven on its real target.

                                                                                      Becomes functional once the real capability exists and is tested on a developer machine and in CI against fakes, emulators or fixtures, with the README saying what the tests stand in for.

                                                                                    2. Functional 89

                                                                                      A real capability, tested on a developer machine and in CI against fakes, emulators or fixtures. No run on the real target (board, machine, CM5, cameras) is recorded; the README says what the tests stand in for.

                                                                                      Becomes established once the repository records a run on its real target (real hardware, a real CM5, a real board) or, for a pure software tool, its whole workflow runs end to end in CI and on a developer machine.

                                                                                    3. Established 18

                                                                                      The repository itself records a run on its real target (real hardware, a real CM5, a real board), or it is a pure software tool whose whole workflow runs end to end in CI and on a developer machine. Passing its own tests is never enough on its own.

                                                                                      Becomes production only after a continuous, unattended deployment with no known open gap.

                                                                                    4. Production 0

                                                                                      A continuous, unattended deployment with no known open gap. Reserved: no repository claims it yet.

                                                                                      The top of the ladder. Nothing advances past here - it just keeps shipping real fixes.

                                                                                    Electro Hobby 3D is four independent engineering ecosystems by the same author: HYDRA-UMC (industrial multi-robot platform), URTC (its universal robot-tool subsystem, an independent product with its own firmware), A.R.M.O.R. (perimeter security and home automation) and EH3D (a PCB, CNC and laser fabrication suite). This dashboard discovers and lists every one of them live; each ecosystem's own family groups are labeled below, and HYDRA-UMC's own deeper architecture is detailed in the section right after this one.

                                                                                    HYDRA-UMC: System architecture

                                                                                    Platform foundation

                                                                                    Raspberry Pi OS ARM64 remains the operating-system base. The HYDRA-UMC layer adds device profiles, diagnostics and service lifecycle.

                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-OS
                                                                                    • CM5 / Linux
                                                                                    • systemd / udev
                                                                                    • MCU / URTC boundary

                                                                                    Contracts and operations

                                                                                    The SDK defines stable data and command contracts; Server, UI and tools use those contracts instead of raw hardware protocols.

                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-SDK
                                                                                    • Server / Studio / Suite
                                                                                    • DSI / mobile / CLI
                                                                                    • Job Dispatcher

                                                                                    Perception and intelligence

                                                                                    Vision and AI are optional capabilities. Their output is validated before it can influence a mission; they are never safety authority.

                                                                                    • Vision Streamer / Node
                                                                                    • Detection HEF
                                                                                    • Cognitive / VLA
                                                                                    • Safety Zones

                                                                                    Engineering and industry

                                                                                    Simulation, telemetry and standards make the physical cell observable, testable and interoperable.

                                                                                    • Twin / Physics / HIL
                                                                                    • Telemetry / DataLake
                                                                                    • OPC-UA / MQTT
                                                                                    • MTConnect / Gateway

                                                                                    Contracts and tests

                                                                                    HYDRA-UMC-SDK holds the v1 JSON Schemas, a Python reference validator, Go, TypeScript and Rust clients that enforce them, conformance fixtures, an OpenAPI slice of the server and a job intake that never runs the same idempotency key twice; a compatibility matrix and a differential test keep validator and schemas in step.

                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-SDK
                                                                                    • JSON Schema / OpenAPI
                                                                                    • Go / TypeScript / Rust clients
                                                                                    • Job intake

                                                                                    Verified updates

                                                                                    HYDRA-UMC-UPDATER installs and updates a repository by cloning, staging, verifying and only then promoting it, so a failed check leaves the live copy untouched; an optional gate refuses a commit without a trusted signature before anything is built. Firmware images are checked with CRC32 and a shared-key HMAC-SHA256; an asymmetric signature is planned, not implemented.

                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-UPDATER
                                                                                    • Staged install
                                                                                    • Signed-commit gate
                                                                                    • CRC32 + HMAC-SHA256

                                                                                    Operations and self-healing

                                                                                    HYDRA-UMC-OPS-AGENT diagnoses and applies only reversible repairs; HYDRA-UMC-NODE-HEALING watches health endpoints and recovers a node through the orchestrator; HYDRA-UMC-LOCAL-TECHNICIAN reads a machine without changing it and assembles evidence bundles; HYDRA-UMC-DEVELOPER-NODE (new, first version) ingests those bundles, runs repro cases a person approved and keeps a cache of checkouts, all closed by default; HYDRA-UMC-DEV-SERVER holds the contracts and limits for development hosts.

                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-OPS-AGENT
                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-NODE-HEALING
                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-LOCAL-TECHNICIAN
                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-DEVELOPER-NODE

                                                                                    Safety, twin and data

                                                                                    HYDRA-UMC-SAFETY-ZONES checks zone breaches and only ever requests a stop; it can optionally read the alarm state of A.R.M.O.R. to inhibit new starts, never to stop a machine that runs. HYDRA-UMC-TWIN and HYDRA-UMC-COGNITIVE-NODE check the readiness of their child services and HYDRA-UMC-PHYSICS-REPLICA computes forward kinematics and joint limits. HYDRA-UMC-DATALAKE stores time series and HYDRA-UMC-DASHBOARD-AI summarises them. HYDRA-UMC-STUDIO-KIT (new, first version) shares sessions, history and an HTTP client between web clients. None of it has met a physical machine.

                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-SAFETY-ZONES
                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-TWIN / COGNITIVE-NODE
                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-DATALAKE / DASHBOARD-AI
                                                                                    • HYDRA-UMC-STUDIO-KIT
                                                                                    Operator interfaces→Server and SDK→CM5-MCU adapter→MCU / URTC / machine
                                                                                    HYDRA-UMC and URTC: HYDRA-UMC is the platform and cell controller. URTC is its universal robot-tool subsystem, with independent firmware and maintenance tools. The MCU remains authoritative for physical limits and safe stop; UI, network and AI cannot bypass that boundary.
                                                                                    URTC: System architecture

                                                                                    Tool-head firmware

                                                                                    An STM32F303 runs each tool head over CAN, reading its own 5-bit hardware address to auto-configure power stages, sensors and safety logic for one of 25 built-in tool profiles.

                                                                                    • STM32F303
                                                                                    • CAN bus
                                                                                    • 5-bit ID matrix
                                                                                    • 25 tool profiles

                                                                                    Expansion and motion

                                                                                    A 20-pin expansion connector adds a second stepper axis or sensor board through one of six interchangeable variants, sharing STEP/DIR/EN wiring between a TMC2209 and a TMC5160 driver.

                                                                                    • TMC2209 / TMC5160
                                                                                    • 6 expansion boards
                                                                                    • F-RAM persistence
                                                                                    • OLED diagnostics

                                                                                    Maintenance tools

                                                                                    URTC-FLASHER updates firmware over CAN without removing the board, URTC-TESTER exercises the protocol end to end and URTC-UPDATER keeps every desktop tool current from GitHub.

                                                                                    • URTC-FLASHER
                                                                                    • URTC-TESTER
                                                                                    • URTC-UPDATER
                                                                                    • CAN-OTA

                                                                                    Vision and operation

                                                                                    URTC-VISION-TOOL adds camera-based tool inspection, URTC-WEB-STUDIO gives it a browser console and URTC-SMART-RACK stores and identifies tool heads between changes.

                                                                                    • URTC-VISION-TOOL
                                                                                    • URTC-WEB-STUDIO
                                                                                    • URTC-SMART-RACK

                                                                                    Contracts and tests

                                                                                    URTC-COMMON writes the CAN protocol once as data, generates a C header, TypeScript and Python modules and a protocol table from it, and keeps the conformance vectors every implementation must reproduce. The firmware and the desktop tools still keep their own copies until each one migrates, so today it is compared against them rather than used by them.

                                                                                    • URTC-COMMON
                                                                                    • CAN spec + generators
                                                                                    • Conformance vectors
                                                                                    • Migration plan

                                                                                    Release assets and signing

                                                                                    Each firmware release is published as GitHub release assets with SHA-256 sidecars and a manifest, and the release tool refuses to publish images signed with the public development key as an official release. The bootloaders check CRC32 and a shared-key HMAC-SHA256; asymmetric signatures are planned, and nothing has been flashed to a real board yet.

                                                                                    • GitHub release assets
                                                                                    • SHA-256 + manifest
                                                                                    • Dev-key release gate
                                                                                    • Asymmetric signing planned

                                                                                    Gateway, shared tools and documentation

                                                                                    URTC-GATEWAY sits in front of the CAN bus for an installation that cannot keep it closed: only identifiers made from the specification cross, dangerous ones are refused unless unlocked, with a payload check, a rate limit and a session key, each one switchable. URTC-DEVTOOLS keeps the shared repository checks as one versioned set and URTC-DOCS holds the architecture, the security baseline and the capability matrix. All three are tested on a computer only.

                                                                                    • URTC-GATEWAY
                                                                                    • URTC-DEVTOOLS
                                                                                    • URTC-DOCS
                                                                                    Tool head→STM32F303 firmware→CAN bus→HYDRA-UMC MCU / host
                                                                                    URTC on its own, and paired with HYDRA-UMC: URTC is an independent, unofficial project - a CAN-based tool-head controller built to work with PAROL6/Faze4-style arms, with its own firmware, hardware and maintenance tools. When it is the tool subsystem of a HYDRA-UMC cell, HYDRA-UMC's own MCU keeps authority over physical limits and safe stop; URTC never bypasses that boundary.
                                                                                    A.R.M.O.R.: System architecture

                                                                                    Network segmentation

                                                                                    Field nodes and cameras sit on their own VLAN with no internet access; the MQTT broker and server live on a core VLAN; Studio and the Android app reach the server from a client VLAN.

                                                                                    • VLAN 10 field
                                                                                    • VLAN 20 core
                                                                                    • VLAN 30 clients
                                                                                    • MQTT, one identity per node

                                                                                    Field nodes

                                                                                    ESP32-S3 radar, solar, electrical, alarm and wall-panel nodes publish sensor and equipment readings or their state; the solar and electrical ones only read, never write to an inverter, battery or meter.

                                                                                    • ARMOR-RADAR
                                                                                    • ARMOR-SOLAR
                                                                                    • ARMOR-ELECTRICAL
                                                                                    • ARMOR-ALARM
                                                                                    • ARMOR-HMI

                                                                                    Perception, never authority

                                                                                    Visual and voice AI recommend a severity or an intent with reasons attached; authorizes_action is always false until the server itself authenticates and confirms.

                                                                                    • ARMOR-SERVER-AI
                                                                                    • ARMOR-VOICE-AI
                                                                                    • Recommend, never act

                                                                                    State and operator consoles

                                                                                    ARMOR-SERVER is the only place that ever touches a camera password or an RTSP address; Studio and the Android app are its authenticated clients, and a phone can set a new node up over Bluetooth alone.

                                                                                    • ARMOR-SERVER
                                                                                    • ARMOR-STUDIO
                                                                                    • ARMOR-ANDROID-CONTROL
                                                                                    • ARMOR-HMI
                                                                                    • BLE set-up only

                                                                                    Contracts and tests

                                                                                    ARMOR-COMMON defines every node message once as a JSON Schema, with a validator that refuses what it does not implement, accepted and rejected conformance vectors that each implementation must pass, the OpenAPI file of the server's routes and the firmware base shared by the five nodes, which a tool keeps identical in each of them.

                                                                                    • ARMOR-COMMON
                                                                                    • JSON Schema / OpenAPI
                                                                                    • Conformance vectors
                                                                                    • Shared firmware base

                                                                                    Signed releases and updates

                                                                                    Node firmware is published with a SHA-256 and an Ed25519 signature, and both a node and ARMOR-SERVER refuse a release without a valid one. The maintenance helper of ARMOR-DEVOPS checks an Ed25519 signature on each service package before unpacking it, which is how ARMOR-STUDIO updates the central machine; the private key never goes to GitHub. A firmware file uploaded by hand is not checked.

                                                                                    • Ed25519 firmware signatures
                                                                                    • ARMOR-DEVOPS signed packages
                                                                                    • ARMOR-STUDIO
                                                                                    • Key never on GitHub

                                                                                    Simulator, network watch and the iPhone client

                                                                                    ARMOR-SIMULATOR produces repeatable telemetry and faults without real nodes; ARMOR-NETWORK watches the network of the test bench and only observes; ARMOR-HARDWARE keeps the enclosure concepts, which need a physical prototype to be validated; ARMOR-IOS-CONTROL is the iPhone port of the Android client, its rules tested without a phone and its screens not yet run on a device. The alarm node can publish its state for HYDRA-UMC-SAFETY-ZONES, which may read it as an optional input.

                                                                                    • ARMOR-SIMULATOR
                                                                                    • ARMOR-NETWORK
                                                                                    • ARMOR-HARDWARE
                                                                                    • ARMOR-IOS-CONTROL
                                                                                    Field nodes and cameras→MQTT broker and server→AI recommendation→Authenticated client session
                                                                                    A.R.M.O.R.'s own boundary: The server is the only component that authorises an action or holds a camera credential. Visual and voice AI only recommend; solar and electrical nodes only read - the rules for switching an electrical source are tested in software but not yet linked to any real hardware.
                                                                                    EH3D: System architecture

                                                                                    One project file and shared crates

                                                                                    EH3D-COMMON defines the .eh3dproj container (a ZIP archive with a hash for every entry and limits that refuse unsafe names), the telemetry types of a machine and the crates the programs share: the scene of a job, the words of the interface, archives, the Bungard file formats, the machine controllers, the height map of the table and the file windows.

                                                                                    • EH3D-COMMON
                                                                                    • .eh3dproj
                                                                                    • SHA-256 integrity
                                                                                    • Shared crates

                                                                                    Readers and documentation

                                                                                    EH3D-CORE-LIBS reads Gerber, Excellon and G-code files from other people, never panics on a damaged one and reports what it could not understand. EH3D-DOCS is the hub: the map of the suite, the architecture and the manuals.

                                                                                    • EH3D-CORE-LIBS
                                                                                    • Gerber / Excellon / G-code
                                                                                    • EH3D-DOCS

                                                                                    CAM and CNC programs

                                                                                    The programs turn PCB layers and images into toolpaths and drive the machine: ISOCAM, DRILLPRO, ROUTEPRO, STENCILCAM, PHOENIX-LASER, AUTOLEVEL and CAM-DEBUGGER, GERBERVIEWER to look at the layers, MOTIONCNC to stream G-code, and BUNGARD-GUI, PNP-MANAGER, VISION-STUDIO and TOOL-MANAGER around them. They depend on the libraries and exchange work through .eh3dproj files, never on each other.

                                                                                    • EH3D-ISOCAM
                                                                                    • EH3D-DRILLPRO
                                                                                    • EH3D-ROUTEPRO
                                                                                    • EH3D-PHOENIX-CNC
                                                                                    • EH3D-GERBERVIEWER

                                                                                    Server and Studio

                                                                                    EH3D-SERVER is the center: it takes the jobs of the programs and the clients, plans them, checks them against the limits of each machine and runs them through its node, a simulator or a GRBL controller. EH3D-STUDIO is the web panel it serves, to set up machines and to prepare and follow jobs.

                                                                                    • EH3D-SERVER
                                                                                    • EH3D-STUDIO
                                                                                    • Simulator / GRBL

                                                                                    Machine nodes

                                                                                    EH3D-NODE-BUNGARD is an ESP32-S3 node that puts the serial port of a Bungard machine on the network; EH3D-NODE-BUNGARD-AUX sits on the drill head (table height, spindle speed and temperature, camera); EH3D-NODE-BUNGARD-HMI and EH3D-NODE-HMI-GUI are the touch screen of the machine. They share the firmware base kept in EH3D-COMMON.

                                                                                    • EH3D-NODE-BUNGARD
                                                                                    • EH3D-NODE-BUNGARD-AUX
                                                                                    • EH3D-NODE-BUNGARD-HMI
                                                                                    • EH3D-NODE-HMI-GUI

                                                                                    Mobile clients, launcher and updater

                                                                                    EH3D-ANDROID-CONTROL and EH3D-IOS-CONTROL are clients of EH3D-SERVER only: they read the fleet and the jobs, prepare jobs and stop them, and never talk to a machine. EH3D-SUITE-LAUNCHER finds the programs by their manifests and starts them, and EH3D-UPDATER keeps every repository of the suite current on the PC.

                                                                                    • EH3D-ANDROID-CONTROL
                                                                                    • EH3D-IOS-CONTROL
                                                                                    • EH3D-SUITE-LAUNCHER
                                                                                    • EH3D-UPDATER
                                                                                    Gerber, Excellon and images→Parsers and CAM tools→G-code and simulation→Machine
                                                                                    EH3D's honest state: EH3D is the newest ecosystem. Each repository declares its own maturity and evidence in its manifest, and the Evidence tab shows them as they are read: most programs are still scaffolding, and nothing is presented as run on a real machine beyond what a repository itself records. A repository planned for the suite appears here as soon as it publishes its manifest.
